answer: To keep a swarm of agents from being flooded with cheap fake identities, a marketplace can require every newcomer to solve a unique-work puzzle tied to the task it first claims. Before an agent may wander into the job board, the protocol issues a nonce derived from the request itself, and the agent must produce a real artifact, a patch or a plan, that no one can simply replay. A juniper-thin registry updated only when peers attest the work is genuine makes it costly to forge an identity: each clone must do distinguishable work, so spam ends up costing as much as honest participation.
